MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  September 16, 2013

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Reardon at 5:07 p.m., on September 16, 2013, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on September 11, 2013, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Leckness
  Council Member Schlicht
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Reardon

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Schlicht

INVOCATION: Council Member Ury

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel: Existing Litigation Subdivision (a) of Section
  54956.9 City of Mission Viejo adv. Capistrano Unified School District; Settlement
  Agreement terms and conditions.

City Council Minutes  1  September 16, 2013
 CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel: Anticipated Litigation Initiation of Litigation
  pursuant to subdivision (c) of Section 54956.9: 4 potential cases.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:08 p.m., Mayor Reardon recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:08 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council addressed two closed session
items. The Council received updates and gave direction to staff but no reportable action
occurred.

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Presentation on the United States Constitution

  The City Council received the presentation from Historian Bob Hayes.

P2. Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition

  Mayor Reardon presented a certificate of commendation to "Noncommissioned Officer of
  the Quarter" Sergeant Neo Aragonespinoza. "Marine of the Quarter" Lance Corporal Shane
  D. Finnel was unable to attend the meeting.

P3. Recognize the Mission Viejo Pony Bronco 11U Southern California Champions

  Mayor Reardon presented commendations to Manager Kyle Schaetzl, Coach Tom Ballogg,
  Coach Casey Simpson and the players.

*Items P4 and P5 were taken out of order.

P5. Recognize the Viejo Little League District 68 12 Year Old All Star Champions

  Mayor Reardon presented certificates of commendation to Manager Fred Noya, Coach Tim
  Fitzgerald, Coach Tim Edwards and the players.

P4. Recognize the Mission Viejo Pony Mustang 9U All Star World Series Champions

  Mayor Reardon presented certificates of commendation to Manager Jimmy Tyler, Coach
  Steve Dietsch, Coach Joe Reick and the players.

City Council Minutes  2  September 16, 2013
 PUBLIC COMMENTS

Elizabeth Busick, M.V.: announced that there is a wonderful pictorial timeline of Mission Viejo
on display at the library through October 3, 2013, and she encouraged teachers and parents to
take their children to visit the display. Mrs. Busick also announced that the Heritage Committee
is seeking residents who are interested in keeping up the history of Mission Viejo. The
committee meets on the first Wednesday of every month at 6:00 p.m. in the Saddleback Room
and she invited those interested to join the next meeting.

Gail Reavis, M.V.: expressed her opposition to the proposed multiple calls party ordinance that
was presented at the last Council Meeting. She referred to a recent newspaper article about a
pastor in San Clemente who was harassed by a neighbor for holding bible studies at his home
and she stated that Mission Viejo's proposal is unnecessary because noise matters are covered by
the State's Penal Code.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: agreed with the prior comments on the multiple calls party
ordinance. He requested that staff give residents an update on his police cost saving ideas and he
asked when he can meet with the new Lieutenant. Mr. Wontrobski also inquired about the status
of the Nadadores' offer to allow residents to use the pool facility and to provide free swimming
lessons.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 9, 11, 12, 14, and 15 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and
  further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of September 3, 2013, as
  presented.

3.  Check Register Dated August 23, 2013 in the Amount of $1,174,657.69
City Council Minutes  3  September 16, 2013
   Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated August 30, 2013 in the Amount of $1,806,524.57

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for July 2013

  Received and filed.

6.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for July 2013

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for July 2013

  Received and filed.

8.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for July 2013

  Received and filed.

10. Review and approval of the Successor Agency’s Administrative Budget of the 13-14B
  Six-Month Fiscal Period of January 1, 2014 to June 30, 2014

  Adopted Successor Agency Resolution 13-04 Approving the Successor Agency's
  Administrative Budget for the 13-14B Six-Month Fiscal Period of January 1, 2014, to June
  30 2014, Pursuant to Health and Safety Code Section 34177(j) Subject to Submittal to and
  Approval by the Oversight Board pursuant to the Dissolution Act.

13. 2014 Orange County International Triathlon in Mission Viejo

  Approved the request submitted by Pelican Coast Events, LLC, to hold the 2014 Orange
  County International Triathlon in Mission Viejo on Sunday, June 1, 2014.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

16. Review of Council Policy 0300-8 Management and Budget Policies

  City Manager Wilberg provided some introductory comments.

City Council Minutes  4  September 16, 2013
   Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report and an overview
  of the General Fund Reserve Policy and estimated Discretionary Reserves at the end
  of fiscal year 2012-13.

  Council Member Schlicht stated that the policy should be to increase our reserves
  percentage and not to do away with the asset replacement minimums policy.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to adopt
  Resolution 13-53 Amending Council Policy 0300-8 Management and Budget Policies.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to move
  the previous question and stop the debate.

  On roll call, said motion (to move the previous question) carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

  On roll call, said MAIN motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

17. Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Review and Request for Direction Relating
  to Kelsey C. Lawrence, a Disapproved Applicant at The Ridge for Purchase of an
  Affordable Unit; Potential Waiver, Interpretation, and/or Amendment of the Policies
  for The Ridge Affordable Housing Program and Eligibility Requirements

  Celeste Brady, Special Counsel, Stradling Yocca Carlson and Rauth, presented a staff
  report and answered questions of the City Council.

  Motion made by Council Member Leckness, seconded by Council Member Ury, to direct
  the MVHA Executive Director and General Counsel to grant a one-time waiver of the
  policy for The Ridge Affordable Housing Program and Eligibility Requirements in
  applicant Kelsey Lawrence's case and allow her to purchase a low-income unit at the Ridge
  condominium complex.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness and Ury
  NOES:  Kelley, Reardon and Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None
City Council Minutes  5  September 16, 2013
 RECESS

At the hour of 9:15 p.m., Mayor Reardon declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at
9:29 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

9.  Northeast Annexation Area / Skyridge Development Project - Boundary Adjustments
  for Inclusion of Newly Annexed Area into Existing City Adopted Road Fee Programs
  and the City’s Special Fire Protection Area

  Council Member Schlicht stated that she removed this item from the Consent Calendar to
  keep consistent with her prior no vote. She also announced that she confirmed with the
  Skyridge developer that they will be disclosing the fire maps.

  By consensus, the City Council directed staff to post the Special Fire Protection Area
  (SFPA) Maps in an easily accessible location on the City's website.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to (1)
  adopt Resolution 13-49 Amending Previously City Adopted Area of Benefit boundaries of
  the Foothill / Eastern Transportation Corridor Fee Program, Foothill Circulation Phasing
  Plan (FCCP), Santiago Canyon Road Fee Program, and the El Toro Road Fee Program to
  include all properties located within the Northeast Annexation Area / Skyridge
  Development Project; and (2) adopted Resolution 13-50 Amending Previously City
  Adopted Boundary of the City's Special Fire Protection Area to include all properties
  located within the Northeast Annexation Area / Skyridge Development Project.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

11. Review and Approval of the Recognized Obligation Payment Schedule for the 13-14B
  Six-Month Fiscal Period of January 1, 2014 to June 30, 2014

  Council Member Schlicht asked for an explanation of the funding listed for the Camino
  Capistrano Bridge improvements.

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas responded that this was an actual
  expenditure of $120. While the City estimated $5,000 for staffing time or consultant
  services, the City only spent $120 and the remaining $4,880 will go back to the County.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Mayor Reardon, to adopt Successor
  Agency Resolution 13-05 Approving Recognized Obligation Payment Schedule for the 13-
  14B Six-Month Fiscal Period of January 1, 2014, to June 30, 2014, Subject to Submittal to
City Council Minutes  6  September 16, 2013
   and Review by the Oversight Board and the Department of Finance ("DOF") pursuant to
  California Health and Safety Code, Division 24, Part 1.85, as amended by Assembly Bill
  1484; Authorize Posting and Transmittal Thereof.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

12. Appropriate Grant Funds for the Building Digital Literacy Services and Collections at
  the Mission Viejo Library Project

  Council Member Schlicht stated that she has great concern about grant money and she is
  especially opposed to this because half of the money will go to a consultant.

  Genesis Hansen, Library Support Services Manager, explained that the consultants' role is
  to provide training for library personnel and parent education classes, as well as
  development of curriculum for hands-on digital literacy classes for parents and
  children. The fees include preparation of material and delivery of the training, as well as
  travel expenses. The budget includes 90 hours for one consultant and 77.5 hours for the
  second consultant at the rate of $100 per hour.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to (1) approve
  appropriation of federal Library Services and Technology Act (LSTA) funds in the amount
  of $40,000, to the Department of Library and Cultural Services FY 13/14 budget; and (2)
  adopt Resolution 13-51 Amending the Library Support Services Budget in the Library
  Fund.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

14. Request for a One-Time Exemption to the "No Alcoholic Beverage Consumption"
  Regulation at City Facilities for the NEC/ITF Wheelchair Tennis Tournaments

  Director of Recreation and Community Services Kelley Doyle requested that one more
  event be added to the request for a waiver of the "No Alcoholic Beverage" regulation. Staff
  is planning a tennis mixer event on Thursday, October 10, 2013, with 22 local tennis
  directors and potential sponsors of the Wheelchair Masters event. Staff is requesting that
  the Council approve the waiver so that beer and wine can be offered at the tennis mixer.

  Motion made by Mayor Reardon, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to approve a one-
  time exemption to the "No Alcoholic Beverage Consumption" regulation at City Facilities
City Council Minutes  7  September 16, 2013
   for the NEC/ITF Wheelchair Tennis Tournaments November 5-11, 2013, and the Tennis
  Mixer on October 10, 2013, at the Marguerite Tennis Pavilion.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

15. Cooperation and Loan Agreement Between the City of Mission Viejo and the
  Successor Agency for Reimbursement of Department of Finance Approved
  Enforceable Obligations, Administrative Costs and/or Project-Related Expenses

  Council Member Ury noted that this agenda item has to do with the City loaning money to
  the Successor Agency and he asked staff to outline the reasons for the recommendation.

  Celeste Brady, Special Counsel, Stradling Yocca Carlson and Rauth, outlined the history of
  the State Department of Finance's demand for monies from the City during the various
  ROPS periods. She stated that the Successor Agency has no powers other than to wind
  down and dissolve the prior redevelopment agency.

  Council Member Ury expressed concern that the City is at the mercy of the State DOF and
  he would like to go to the private equity market to borrow money so that the State cannot
  take the money from the City as they have done in the past.

  Mrs. Brady, City Attorney Curley and Director Dyas explained that the Successor Agency
  does not have the authority to borrow money from anyone other than the City. They further
  explained that the City would not be able to borrow money from a commercial lender for
  expenses that have already been made.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to (1)
  adopt Successor Agency Resolution 13-06 Approving a Cooperation Agreement (A13-38)
  and Loan Agreement Pursuant to Health & Safety Code Section 34173(h) By and Between
  the City of Mission Viejo and the Successor Agency and Making Certain Findings in
  Accordance Therewith; and (2) adopt City Council Resolution 13-52 Approving a
  Cooperation Agreement and Loan Agreement Pursuant to Health & Safety Code Section
  34173(h) By and Between the City of Mission Viejo and the Successor Agency.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  8  September 16, 2013
 MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

18. Investment Advisory Commission Vacancy

  Council Member Ury asked that this item be continued to the next City Council Meeting.

19. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that most Mission Viejo residents are uninformed and
  believe that firefighters are paid between $65,000 and $75,000 a year. He stated that he did
  his own total wage analysis on salary and benefits, concluding that the average firefighter
  earns $212,000 a year.

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley presented the report.

20. Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Reardon presented the report.

21. San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Reardon presented the report.

22. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

23. SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley presented the report.

Orange County Vector Control District

Council Member Leckness presented a report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

City Manager Wilberg reminded the Council that he and several staff members will be at the
League of Cities conference from Wednesday through the end of the week and he will be at a
City Manager's conference next week.

Council Member Schlicht asked if it was a smooth transition with the new school crossing guard
company.

City Council Minutes  9  September 16, 2013
 City Manager Wilberg responded that staff and motorcycle officers have been monitoring all of
the crossing guard locations to make sure that there are no problems. There were some issues
with former crossing guards, re-hired by the new company, who quit the week before school but
overall, it was a relatively smooth transition and staff will continue to monitor.

City Attorney’s Report

City Attorney Bill Curley discussed recent medical marijuana dispensary bills that were
considered in Sacramento. Several of the bills failed to move out of committee and he assured
the Council that the City's ordinance is solid and is supported by the State Supreme Court. Mr.
Curley noted that there are still some concerns with the staggering amount of money behind the
medical marijuana industry and agricultural companies are starting to see how much money there
is to be made.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

24. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Leckness

Council Member Leckness discussed an upcoming event "Secrets to Business Success Overseas"
which will be held on September 27, 2013, from 10:00 a.m. to noon at the Mission Viejo
Country Club. The seminar will feature detailed information about exporting to China and what
products and services are needed there most. Council Member Leckness discussed his recent trip
to China where he learned that Chinese consumers love American products and there is money to
be made. He also shared an ABC News video which revealed that made-in-America products
have increased 540% in the past 10 years in China and the program outlined the success of
several Americans who are selling products abroad. Council Member Leckness stated that he
hopes to inspire local business owners and entrepreneurs to attend the event so they can learn
how to sell their own products overseas.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht stated that changing the budget policy this evening to eliminate target
levels for a policy that requires no minimum balance in the asset replacement reserves was a bad
decision by the Council majority. She stated that asking her to find the $7.7 million shortfall is
dodging reality and that the Council should focus on infrastructure maintenance. Council
Member Schlicht noted that this is why she did not approve the budget as she feels there is too
much social spending at the expense of the infrastructure. Council Member Schlicht read a
prepared statement regarding her assertion that Council Member Ury and Mayor Reardon
violated the Brown Act when responding to an email from the City Clerk regarding the June 3,
2013, Council Meeting Minutes. She stated that the Minutes were politically written and she
feels the two Council Members flagrantly violated the Brown Act and she presented her backup
City Council Minutes  10  September 16, 2013
 documentation for the public record. Council Member Schlicht outlined upcoming meetings
regarding the shutdown of the San Onofre Nuclear Generating Station as follows: (1) September
26, Nuclear Regulatory Commission hearing from 6:00 to 9:00 p.m. at the La Costa Hotel, 2100
Costa del Mar Blvd., Carlsbad; (2) October 1, California Public Utilities Commission hearing
beginning at 1:00 p.m. for a press conference by members of the Coalition to Decommission San
Onofre and from 2:00 to 5:00 p.m. and 6:30 to 9:30 p.m., a CPUC hearing at Al Bahr Shriners
building, 5440 Kearny Mesa Road, San Diego; and (3) October 19, Symposium - Coalition to
Decommission San Onofre - from 1:30 to 4:30 p.m. at the Center for Spiritual Living, 1201
Puerta del Sol, San Clemente. Council Member Schlicht announced that the Saddleback
Republican Assembly will meet on September 19 at 7:00 p.m. at the Murray Community Center
with guest speaker, Brad Dacus, Founder and President of Pacific Justice Institute. Also
SOC912 will be meeting on September 20 at the Murray Community Center and they will show
a documentary entitled "They Came to America, Part 2." Council Member Schlicht discussed
her attendance at the Patriots Day event where she presented information on 911 hero Todd
Beamer who died on Flight 93 on September 11, 2001. Referring to presentations earlier in the
meeting, she commended the City's adopted Marines for their service and for defending our
Constitution. She also thanked the parents and coaches who were honored for helping the kids
with their sports and instilling teamwork, good sportsmanship and for teaching respect and
discipline. Council Member Schlicht announced that she attended recent sporting events
including the Diablos football game on September 6 and she noted that she will watch the
Diablos play again this week at Cerritos College. Council Member Schlicht asked the Mayor to
adjourn the meeting in memory of those who died in today's attack at the Naval Shipyard in
Washington D.C. and she concluded with a quote from William Howard Taft: "Constitutions are
checks upon the hasty action of the majority. They are the self-imposed restraints of a whole
people upon a majority of them to secure sober action and a respect for the rights of the
minority."

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury thanked Jerry Hill and his entire staff for their help in arranging his son
Alex's upcoming Eagle Scout project.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley commended City Clerk Karen Hamman for a nice job on the Outlook
magazine. She stated that the magazine highlights good news about things that are going on in
the City and it showcases the talents of the City Clerk. She also announced that there will be an
American Red Cross Blood Drive on Friday, September 20, 2013, from 12:00 to 6:00 p.m. in the
Saddleback Room at City Hall. Participants can make an appointment on the Red Cross website
or call her to register. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley thanked Anna T. Boyce for helping with each of
the Red Cross blood drives and for recruiting volunteers to assist. Mrs. Kelley announced that
the Community of Character word for the month of September is responsibility and the word for
October is respect. The Character Committee will be screening the movie "Bully" to support
National Bullying Prevention Month in October and to support the effort to prevent bullying in
the City of Mission Viejo. The film follows 5 children and their families over the course of a
year and the Character Committee is hopping to have participation and input from every one of
City Council Minutes  11  September 16, 2013
 Mission Viejo's schools, whether it is a student, a teacher, an administrator, a parent, or a School
Resource Officer. The movie will be shown in the Council Chamber on Sunday October 20,
2013, and Mayor Pro Tem Kelley encouraged parents to learn about bullying, stay involved in
their children's lives and to try and attend the screening of this important film.

Mayor Reardon

Mayor Reardon commended Council Member Schlicht and Council Member Leckness for their
part in the Patriots Day ceremony. At the event, Council Member Leckness shared a very
moving story about the chirping sound that emanates from a firefighter's jacket when there is no
movement and how mass chirping could be heard around ground zero after the towers came
down on 9/11. Council Member Schlicht talked about the terrorists and how they tried to divide
the country but instead brought us together. Mayor Reardon announced that resident Bob Hayes
is conducting a series on the Constitution on September 19 and 26 from 4:00 to 5:00 p.m. at the
Murray Center. Also, resident Dave Dickey will present an economics forum on September 19,
September 26 and October 3 at the Murray center. She also announced that the cities of San
Juan Capistrano and San Clemente will get some traffic relief when the Antonio/La Pata
extension is complete. This is a much-needed project that will enhance mobility in South
County. Mayor Reardon reminded residents that October is the month for the annual drug walk
and she discussed her recent television interview with Andrew Presta about his struggle with
prescription drug addiction. She also thanked everyone for their prayers for her grandson Noah
who was ill and hospitalized recently. Mayor Reardon drew attention to an article in the new
issue of Outlook about the SCAT volunteers and she echoed Mayor Pro Tem Kelly's
compliments to City Clerk Hamman for doing a great job with the magazine. In closing, Mayor
Reardon announced that she will adjourn the meeting in memory of those who lost their lives
today in the Naval Shipyard shooting and in memory of Ron Saltzgiver.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 11:17 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor Reardon adjourned the meeting in memory of the victims of the Washington
D.C. Naval Shipyard shootings and Ron Saltzgiver, to Monday, October 7, 2013, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of October 7, 2013

City Council Minutes  12  September 16, 2013
